leftEvidence.role: Law, righteousness, and the inner life
leftEvidence.title: Vows give way to unadorned yes and no

points.label: Event action and claim
points.left: Jesus recalls commands about vows and says not to swear by heaven, earth, Jerusalem, or one’s head.
points.right: The LORD forbids theft, deception, false swearing, oppression, injustice, slander, hatred, vengeance, and grudges.

points.label: Response and consequence
points.left: Speech is narrowed to a reliable yes or no.
points.right: The paragraph commands rebuke and love for one’s neighbor as oneself.

payload.posture: Leviticus forbids false swearing; Matthew rejects supporting ordinary truthfulness with invoked objects.

rightEvidence.title: Truth, judgment, inner hatred, and neighbor love stand together

payload.tension: Matthew’s broader instruction cannot be reduced to the Leviticus prohibition alone.
payload.title: False swearing and reliable speech
